newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds advance in directional trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds advance in directional trade.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities were higher in line with Treasuries by late afternoon, after weaker-than-expected economic data buoyed prices earlier in day, market sources said.
Mortgages got a directional lift after Treasuries were spurred by unexpectedly weak October housing starts during the morning trading session, traders said.
"We got help from a weak (housing starts) number," said one regional trader. But most of mortgage activity has been directional, he said.
The U.S. Commerce Department reported total housing starts fell 5.1 percent to an annualized 1.366 million rate, the lowest rate since 1.351 million in October 1995.
A recent Reuters poll showed experts forecast the annual rate of total housing starts for October to have risen to 1.443 million units.
By late afternoon Tuesday, current-coupon pass-throughs trailed the 10-year Treasury note by a couple of ticks, rising 7/32 to 8/32.
The 10-year Treasury note was up 9/32 at 102-15/32 to yield 6.16 percent.
Specifically, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.0 percent coupons were up 8/32 at 99-03/32, yielding 102 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent coupons were up 5/32 at 100-24/32, and Freddie Mac 7.0's jumped 8/32 to 99-06/32.
No major bid lists were cited, traders said.
"Its been pretty quiet today," said one New York-based trader. "Other than some light odd-lot trading, there was nothing much going on," he said.
